intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Overview
paragraphs: More than just reaching Everest Base Camp, this trek offers amazing experiences from start to finish. It is also one of the most classic routes in Nepal.

This itinerary is designed around a trekking route from Lukla to Everest Base Camp to Pheriche, maximizing the potential for a transformative experience on the trail. From Pheriche, we arrange a heli-tour back to Kathmandu to minimize some of the toil in hiking down from Pheriche to Lukla and expedite the return to the city. This shortens the overall itinerary by 2-3 days.

groups.title: Acclimatization Day Hike
prose: On clear days, catch the first views of Aba Dablam and Mount Everest while we embark on our first acclimatization hike of the itineary. This hike will proceed to Khumjung Village and return to Namche Bazaar.

prose: This is approximately a 5-6 hour trek with our sleeping altitude in Deboche being approximately 3860m or 12660ft.

groups.title: Acclimatization Day - Hike/Climb
prose: This is a round-trip, steep hike (dare we say climb) to the Nagarjunga viewpoint.

groups.title: Trek to Lobuche
prose: This trek is approximately 4-5 hours and our sleeping altitude in Lobuche is approximately 4910m or 16104ft.

groups.title: Kala Pathar, Sunset views of Everest, and Gorak Shep
prose: Trek to Kala Pathar (5620m or 18433ft) for a sunset view of Everest and return to Gorak Shep for the evening. The total duration is approximately 8-9 hours and the sleeping altitude in Gorak Shep is approximately 5180m or 16990ft.

highlights.title: Lukla - The Flight of a Lifetime
highlights.body: Lukla is one of the most thrilling airport locations in the world. The whole experience is unlike anything else. Situated on a mountainside, right in the midst of stunning Himalayan peaks, this airport serves the entire region as there are no roads that reach Lukla. One must fly or walk to get there. Yak caravans come all the way to the door to load gear and supplies headed toward Namche Bazaar and beyond. Once we've landed, we will gather our bags, stop for a quick tea, and begin trekking down the valley toward our first evening destination, Phakding.
highlights.imageAlt: Lukla - The Flight of a Lifetime

highlights.title: Working Our Way Up
highlights.body: Slowly, slowly. This is the mantra for trekking up the Khumbu Valley. There will be several steep switchbacks throughout the valley and the first one is encountered on the way up to Namche Bazaar. Slow and steady is the name of the game. Our itineraries are designed around and average of 4-6 hours of trekking each day. We move at a calculated pace so we do not burn you out too early or rush the acclimatization process. This is by design. As we move from village to village, we leave each morning after breakfast, stop for lunch along the way, and arrive mid afternoon to rest for the next day.

highlights.title: Acclimatization Days
highlights.body: Climb high, sleep low. On multiple occasions throughout the itinerary, we schedule acclimatization hikes to help facilitate our adjustment to the high altitudes encountered throughout the trek. On these days, we will depart the village, climb to higher destinations (often viewpoints to see peaks like Everest, Ama Dablam, etc...), possibly visit other villages, and then return to the same place we began for a second night of sleep at the same resting altitude. This helps the body adjust and reduces the risk of altitude sickness as we keep moving up the valley.

highlights.title: Quit Yakking, Start Packing
highlights.body: Once we depart Namche Bazaar, the serious work begins and we will travel through Deboche, Dingboche, and Lobuche. Don't think of this as busy work. Each of these stops and the trail segments between them are valuable experiences and they delight the senses. Along the way we move beyond forests to being well above the tree line and your surroundings will start to match what you've imagined the Himalayas look like. It's like being in another world!

included: Accommodations: 3-5 star accommodations are available in Kathmandu. We generally choose 3 start accomodations in Boudha at the beginning of the tour and a 4 star hotel in Thamel on the back end. We will confirm this type of selection with you in the booking/payment process.

Meals: In the itinerary you will see B - Breakfast, L - Lunch, and/or D - Dinner indicated on each day. The presence of any of these letters indicates which meals are included on the day. For example: B / L / D means all three meals of the day will be provided while B / - / D means breakfast and dinner are provided as part of the package but lunch is on your own.
Domestic transportation: All ground and air travel within Nepal as indicated in the itinerary
excluded: Alcohol: We strongly encourage minimizing or eliminating alcohol while acclimatizing. Should you choose to drink alcohol when appropriate, you may do so but must pay your alcohol tab at the close of the meal.

Tips: It is customary to tip all senior guides, junior guides, and porters. We will provide information about the tipping culture in Nepal so you can make informed decisions regarding when to tip and how much to tip.
Clothing and Equipment: We do not provide your gear but do have a packing list to help you prepare. We are happy to answer any questions you have and make recommendations if you need assistance.

cards.title: What to expect in Kathmandu
cards.body: You may have started this journey with an interest in the mountains of Nepal but no trip is complete without a good experience in Kathmandu. From the moment you meet your guide at the airport in Kathmandu, you are in good hands. There is no need to navigate the airport scene or figure out how to find your hotel in the back alleys of Boudha or Thamel. Don't worry, there is ample opportunity to get out and explore. You will be able to immerse yourself in the bustling network of alleys, streets, and buildings as you take in the city. Our guides, however, take care of the details so you can take in the surroundings. Your time in Kathmandu will also include good food, getting to know your guide, and an orientation for the trek. By the time we depart the city, everyone will be prepared for the mountains and your cultural curiosity will have been stoked.

cards.title: Everest Base Camp and Kala Pathar
cards.body: Once in the Base Camp region, we include two days in this itinerary to maximize your experience. From base camp, Mt. Everest is barely visible because of the way surrounding peaks block the view. For this reason, we plan a climb up Kala Pathar to catch the evening light on the slopes of Everest. A subsequent visit to Base Camp will put you on the Khumbu Glacier and provide you time to explore a portion of the site before we head back down the valley toward Pheriche.

cards.title: Soar through the Himalayas
cards.body: After one night in Pheriche, you will return to Kathmandu via helicopter. This shortens the trekking itinerary by two full days, allows for a more reliable departure from the region, and on clear days it provides stunning views of the mountains on the way back to Kathmandu.
